headline: Only ~120-122 of the 600 food-aid trucks a day agreed under the ceasefire are entering Gaza, as winter floods hit 70,000 tents
dek: Baghaei said Gaza faces 'serious problems' in the cold of winter without minimum living conditions: of the 600 food-aid trucks supposed to enter Gaza daily under the Sharm el-Sheikh understanding, only about 120 to 122 trucks are arriving daily, 'which does not meet the needs of nearly two million…
sources: Esmaeil Baghaei, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman, weekly press conference, via Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: Is Gaza starving because Israel is deliberately choking the crossings at ~120 of 600 trucks a day -- or because the crossings cannot safely move more while the war's wreckage and looting continue?

sections.what_happened: Baghaei said Gaza faces 'serious problems' in the cold of winter without minimum living conditions: of the 600 food-aid trucks supposed to enter Gaza daily under the Sharm el-Sheikh understanding, only about 120 to 122 trucks are arriving daily, 'which does not meet the needs of nearly two million Palestinian refugees'. Context: first winter storm flooded 70,000+ tents (Gaza Government Media Office, Nov 7-8; already recorded 0400-01); 1.98 million people need shelter help (UNRWA); only 17% of winter shelter needs met (IOM, Oct); 8,600 emergency shelter kits blocked; 60,000 mobile homes and 200,000 tents blocked from entry, only 20,000 tents allowed in (AJ Nov 9 feature).
sections.what_verified: The 120-122/day figure: 1 declared-tier family (Al Jazeera, T2) carrying the spokesman's own statement -- primary_source_single_family: true. The 600/day commitment is corroborated separately: Mohammed Salha, Palestinian NGO Network director, told Al Jazeera Nov 7 that only 180-200 trucks enter daily vs 600 agreed; Drop Site News (Nov 3) reported ~200/day vs 600 agreed; Palestinian factions' joint statement Nov 8 demanded at least 600 trucks/day; Gaza Government Media Office said aid entered at 20.3% of the agreed rate in October. Drop Site News and Maktoob have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Figures differ by source and date: Salha (Nov 7, via AJ) said 180-200 trucks/day with only ~40 carrying humanitarian aid -- higher than Baghaei's 120-122, same direction. COGAT (Israeli aid-coordination body) did not respond to the flooding (Maktoob); Israel justifies restrictions on dual-use and looting grounds. Baghaei is Iran's spokesman, not a neutral aid monitor -- his number is a claim, not a count. No UN/OCHA daily truck count was in-window to settle 120 vs 200.
sections.why_matters: 600 trucks promised. 120 arriving. 70,000 tents underwater: the number that shows the ceasefire's aid promise is not being kept -- as winter hits Gaza.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW -- Iran FM spokesman: only ~120-122 of the 600 food-aid trucks a day agreed under the ceasefire are entering Gaza, as winter floods hit 70,000 tents

totw_analysis: Our read: 600 trucks promised. 120 arriving. 70,000 tents underwater: the number that shows the ceasefire's aid promise is not being kept -- as winter hits Gaza. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Gaza starving because Israel is deliberately choking the crossings at ~120 of 600 trucks a day -- or because the crossings cannot safely move more while the war's wreckage and looting continue?
